title: Constructible sheaves form a weak Serre subcategory
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring, and let $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ be the abelian category of sheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules on the small etale site $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Call an object of $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ constructible if it is constructible in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] (the notion of [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]: a finite partition of $X$ into locally closed constructible strata on whose inverse images the sheaf is finite locally constant). Then the constructible sheaves are closed under kernels, cokernels and extensions in $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$: (1) for a morphism $\varphi\colon\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ in $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ between constructible sheaves, $\operatorname{Ker}(\varphi)$ and $\operatorname{Coker}(\varphi)$ are constructible; (2) for a short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal E\to\mathcal G\to0$ in $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ with $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal G$ constructible, $\mathcal E$ is constructible.

note:
*Source:* Stacks Project, Etale Cohomology, Lemma 59.71.6, [Tag
03RZ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03RZ). The pro-etale counterpart
of the weak-Serre assertion, stated there for a Noetherian coefficient ring,
is Stacks Project, Section 61.27, [Tag
09AI](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09AI); the form used here is the
etale statement just cited, for a finite ring $\Lambda$.

proof.text: *Setting.* In case (1) let $\varphi\colon\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ be the morphism and put $\mathcal K=\operatorname{Ker}(\varphi)$, $\mathcal Q=\operatorname{Coker}(\varphi)$; in case (2) let $0\to\mathcal F\xrightarrow{a}\mathcal E\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal G\to0$ be the sequence. In both cases $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal G$ are constructible [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]: there are stratifications $(\iota_k\colon Z_k\to X)_{k<n}$ and $(\kappa_l\colon W_l\to X)_{l<m}$ of the scheme $X$ [def-constructible-stratification], with strata $T_k=\iota_k(Z_k)$ and $T'_l=\kappa_l(W_l)$ constructible subsets of $X$, such that every $\iota_k^{-1}\mathcal F$ and every $\kappa_l^{-1}\mathcal G$ is finite locally constant with finite values (an etale covering on whose members it is isomorphic to a constant sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules with finite value). Stacks first replaces $X$ by the members of an affine open covering, because its Definition 03RW asks for a partition of every affine open; the notion of [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] asks for one finite partition of $X$ itself, so that reduction is not needed here, and the second reduction of the proof (to the members of one finite partition on which both sheaves are finite locally constant) is made directly on $X$ in the next steps. (Stacks proves the weak Serre property via the criterion Homology 0754; kernels, cokernels and extensions, the three closure properties of that criterion, are exactly the statement here.)

*The common partition.* By [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-stratification-intersection], applied to $(\iota_k)_k$ and $(\kappa_l)_l$, the family $(\mu_{k,l}\colon V_{k,l}=Z_k\times_XW_l\to X)_{(k,l)}$, $\mu_{k,l}=\iota_k\circ\mathrm{pr}_1$, is a stratification of $X$ with strata $T_k\cap T'_l$, each a constructible subset of $X$, and it refines both $(\iota_k)_k$ and $(\kappa_l)_l$ [def-constructible-refines]. This is Stacks' 'finite partition of $X$ by constructible locally closed subschemes on which $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal G$ are ... locally constant'; the next step checks the last clause.

*$\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal G$ are finite locally constant on every part.* By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-constant-module-values], (1)$\Rightarrow$(2), each $\iota_k^{-1}\mathcal F$ and each $\kappa_l^{-1}\mathcal G$ is finite locally constant in the sense of [def-constructible-finite-locally-constant] (locally constant with finite geometric stalks) for the coefficient category of $\Lambda$-modules. Since $(\mu_{k,l})$ refines $(\iota_k)$, [lemma-constructible-of-refines] gives that every $\mu_{k,l}^{-1}\mathcal F$ is finite locally constant; since it refines $(\kappa_l)$, the same lemma gives that every $\mu_{k,l}^{-1}\mathcal G$ is finite locally constant. ($\mu^{-1}$ is the inverse image of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], acting on sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules, which is the pullback $\mu^*$ of the blueprint lemma.)

*Inverse image to a part is exact.* Fix $(k,l)$ and write $\mu=\mu_{k,l}$, $V=V_{k,l}$. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] (2), (3), with $R=\Lambda$, $\mu^{-1}\colon\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Mod(V_{\Et},\Lambda)$ is an additive exact functor (it preserves finite limits and finite colimits). Hence the canonical comparison maps are isomorphisms $\mu^{-1}\operatorname{Ker}(\varphi)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Ker}(\mu^{-1}\varphi)$ and $\operatorname{Coker}(\mu^{-1}\varphi)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mu^{-1}\operatorname{Coker}(\varphi)$, and $0\to\mu^{-1}\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\mu^{-1}a}\mu^{-1}\mathcal E\xrightarrow{\mu^{-1}b}\mu^{-1}\mathcal G\to0$ is a short exact sequence in $\Mod(V_{\Et},\Lambda)$.

*Kernels, cokernels and extensions on a part (Stacks 03RX (3), via Modules on Sites 093U).* By step 3, $\mu^{-1}\mathcal F$ and $\mu^{-1}\mathcal G$ are finite locally constant sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on $V_{\Et}$, $\Lambda$ finite. By [lemma-constructible-flc-serre], $\operatorname{Ker}(\mu^{-1}\varphi)$ and $\operatorname{Coker}(\mu^{-1}\varphi)$ are finite locally constant (kernel and cokernel clauses), and the middle term $\mu^{-1}\mathcal E$ of the short exact sequence of step 4 is finite locally constant (extension clause). By the isomorphisms of step 4 and [lemma-constructible-iso-invariance], $\mu^{-1}\mathcal K$ and $\mu^{-1}\mathcal Q$ are finite locally constant. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-constant-module-values], (2)$\Rightarrow$(1), $\mu^{-1}\mathcal K$, $\mu^{-1}\mathcal Q$ and $\mu^{-1}\mathcal E$ are finite locally constant with finite values, as [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] (b) asks.

source.place: Lemma 03RZ, proof of (3): 'Thus we may apply Lemma 03RX to conclude'; Lemma 03RX (lemma-kernel-finite-locally-constant) (3), proved by Modules on Sites Lemma 093U (sites-modules-lemma-kernel-finite-locally-constant)

proof.text: *Conclusion.* The stratification $(\mu_{k,l})_{(k,l)}$ of step 2 has constructible locally closed strata, and by step 5 the inverse images of $\mathcal K$, $\mathcal Q$ (case (1)) and of $\mathcal E$ (case (2)) to every stratum are finite locally constant with finite values. So $\mathcal K$, $\mathcal Q$ and $\mathcal E$ are constructible by the definition [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf].

blueprint_sketch.statement:
Let $\mathcal A=\mathrm{Mod}_\Lambda$ with $\Lambda$ a finite ring. The
kernel and the cokernel of a morphism between constructible sheaves on
$\et X$, finite direct sums of constructible sheaves, and the middle term of
a short exact sequence whose outer terms are constructible, are
constructible. Consequently the constructible sheaves form a weak Serre
subcategory of $\shv{\et X}$. (The kernel and cokernel statements are
formalised, for any ring $\Lambda$, as are the instances
`IsClosedUnderKernels` and `IsClosedUnderCokernels` of
`Etale.constructibleSheaf`; the extension statement is not.)
blueprint_sketch.proof:
Let $\varphi\colon\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$ be a morphism of constructible
sheaves. By [lemma-constructible-common-refinement] and
[lemma-constructible-of-refines] there is one stratification
$(\iota_k\colon Z_k\to X)_k$ such that all $\iota_k^*\mathcal F$ and
$\iota_k^*\mathcal F'$ are finite locally constant. Since $\iota_k^*$ is
exact, $\iota_k^*\ker\varphi=\ker(\iota_k^*\varphi)$ and
$\iota_k^*\operatorname{coker}\varphi=\operatorname{coker}(\iota_k^*\varphi)$
are finite locally constant by [lemma-constructible-flc-serre], so
$\ker\varphi$ and $\operatorname{coker}\varphi$ are constructible with
respect to the same stratification. The same argument, using exactness of
$\iota_k^*$ and the extension part of [lemma-constructible-flc-serre],
handles extensions, and [lemma-constructible-flc-biproduct] handles
finite direct sums. A full subcategory of an abelian category closed under
kernels, cokernels and extensions is a weak Serre subcategory.

blueprint_sketch.statement:
For a scheme $T$ and a finite ring $\Lambda$, the constructible
$\Lambda$-module sheaves on $T_{\Et}$ form a weak Serre subcategory of
$\Mod(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$: kernels, cokernels, and extensions of constructible
sheaves are constructible.

*Source:* Stacks Project, Etale Cohomology, Lemma 59.71.6, [Tag
03RZ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03RZ). The pro-etale counterpart
of the weak-Serre assertion, stated there for a Noetherian coefficient ring,
is Stacks Project, Section 61.27, [Tag
09AI](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09AI); the form used here is the
etale statement just cited, for a finite ring $\Lambda$.
blueprint_sketch.proof:
Work on an affine open of $T$, and refine the finitely many partitions of
the given constructible sheaves to one common partition, as in the
definition of a constructible complex. Inverse image to a part is exact, by
the stalkwise exactness of geometric stalks. It suffices to prove the
assertions for finite locally constant sheaves on each part, locally for the
topology of the small etale site.

For a map between two such sheaves, trivialize both near a geometric point.
The images of the finitely many elements of the first constant module are
sections of the second. After an etale refinement each is a specified
constant section. The map is then induced by a map of finite modules, whose
kernel and cokernel give the constant kernel and cokernel sheaves. These
descriptions prove the first two assertions.

Consider an extension $0\to F'\to F\to F''\to0$ with $F'$ and $F''$ finite
locally constant. Fix a geometric point $\bar t$ and trivialize both outer
sheaves on an etale neighbourhood. By the exactness of geometric stalks, the
middle stalk $B=F_{\bar t}$ is an extension of two finite modules and is
finite. Represent each of its finitely many elements by a section of $F$ on
a common pointed etale neighbourhood. All addition, zero and
scalar-multiplication relations of $B$ hold after a further common
refinement: there are only finitely many relations since $B$ and $\Lambda$
are finite, and equality in a stalk means equality on such a neighbourhood.
Also impose the finitely many equalities identifying the chosen sections of
the submodule with the constant sections of $F'$, and their images with the
constant sections of $F''$. We obtain a map from the constant exact sequence
of stalk modules to the given exact sequence, which is the identity on the
outer terms. The kernel--cokernel argument for a map of short exact
sequences makes the middle map an isomorphism; equivalently, apply the same
argument on every stalk and conservativity of geometric stalks. Thus $F$ is
finite locally constant near every point. Applying this on the common
partition proves extension closure and completes the proof.
